text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Defence Minister Andrus Oovel rejected Culture Minister Jaak Allik's criticism of Estonia's aspirations to NATO, saying Allik is confusing security within and outside Estonia.
- The second stage of the Baltic Challenge military exercise began Sunday in Paldiski, simulating rescue operations after an earthquake.
- A 48-member Estonian team left for rescue exercises in Iceland.
- The Unrepresented Nations Organisation failed to elect a new secretary general and postponed the election until January.
- The death sentence in Estonia should be abolished before the European Union meeting in December, the chairman of the parliamentary legal commission said in an interview.
- A plaque to dead Chechen leader Dzhokhar Dudayev was unveiled at the house where Dudayev worked in 1987-91 while he was the head of the Soviet Army garrison in Tartu.
- The state chancellery's lawsuit against a member of northestern Maardu city council may become the first case of a council member losing his post for not knowing Estonian.

- The central Bank of Estonia experts predict export growth to be 1.35 times higher than the growth of imports. A survey by SAAR-POLL showed exporting companies were confident and optimistic about their chances, especially in CIS countries.
